checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One finished 16:9 image with original left and renovated right
must.why: Image is 16:9 but the left panel is not the original; it is a different, already-renovated white kitchen cropped and merged.

must.item: Left photo retains brown cabinets, beige tiles, original clutter
must.why: Left shows white cabinets, white tiles, empty beige counter; original brown cabinets and clutter are gone.

must.item: Right panel has white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles, uncluttered
must.why: Right side shows white shaker cabinets, light wood counters, white tiles, clean counters (the standalone makeover is solid).

must.item: Generated kitchen preserves geometry and viewpoint
must.why: The makeover keeps the layout, sink, window and camera angle close to the original.
Both labels are legible in dark banners, correctly placed over their panels.

faults.what: The 'Before' panel is not the user's original kitchen: brown cabinets, beige tiles and clutter were replaced by a white renovated look, so it misrepresents the original.
The left panel's sink is cut off and mashed against the right panel, with a distorted layout and a second sink missing. The two halves are awkwardly overlapped with a white divider line.
Both panels appear to be partial crops of the same scene, so the comparison is not clean and has AI artefacts (altered cabinet drawer positions).
The label banners cover parts of the cabinets.

summary: The final before-and-after image shows a renovated-looking kitchen on both sides, with the user's real brown, cluttered original missing from the "Before" panel, so it fails the core purpose despite correct labels.
